column1: # THE SWEEP IS FINISHED, AND THEN PART OF IT WAS WITHDRAWN. Every authoring component Core Keeper
# ships was written by the framework and every field on every one of them was reachable. Then the
# last group was re-checked against what the game actually loads, and eighteen of those components
# turned out to be reachable on paper only: they were written onto a prefab the mod pipeline throws
# away, so no creator answer on them ever changed a running game.
#   377 authoring types in the SDK
#   357 are MonoBehaviour components the framework writes and the game reads
#    18 are components a mod cannot ship at all — the game's own rule-table carrier and its own
#       player. Five of them changed rules that CAN be reached another way, and those five moved
#       to World Rules or to the assets that already owned them; the rest have no seam. The list
#       below says which is which for every one.
#     2 are not components at all, so there is nothing to author:
#         PugMod.IAuthoring         an interface
#         PugMod.ModAPIAuthoring    PugMod's baking hook — a plain class, not a MonoBehaviour,
#                                   never put on a prefab, and its two members are get-only
#                                   properties rather than serialized fields
# A field is only counted as covered when a verified chain carries it into play, so the honest
# number is field coverage over the 357, not over the 375. Re-check with:
#     bash Docs/audit-field-coverage.sh
# The last 25, and what became of each:
# ---- the game's own tables and prefab lists ----
# WITHDRAWN. These thirteen rows were once "covered" by a prefab a mod could not ship. Core
# Keeper drops any object without IEntityMonoBehaviourData twice on the way in, and the object
# database keeps whichever copy of an object arrived first — which is always vanilla's. So none of
# these ever reached a running game, and generating them was retired.
# What actually reaches the game, and where it now lives:
#   LootTableAuthoring                served by the loot tables and Drop Location, which patch
#                                     LootTableConverter.Convert
#   ConditionsTableAuthoring          served by the conditions, which patch
#                                     ConditionsTableConverter.Convert
#   EnvironmentSpawnObjectsTable-     served by the spawn and respawn rules, which patch
#     Authoring                       EnvironmentSpawnObjectsTableConverter.Convert
#   BiomesTableAuthoring              vanilla's own radial ring worldgen, not dimension biomes;
#                                     dimension biomes are served by the biome registry
#   PugDatabaseAuthoring              every framework generator already registers its objects
#                                     through the mod pipeline; a second database is a hard error
#   UpgradeCostsTableAuthoring        World Rules ▸ "What upgrading costs"
#                                     (DimensionUpgradeCostRegistry, prefix on
#                                     UpgradeCostsTableConverter.Convert)
#   FishingTableAuthoring             World Rules ▸ "What fishing catches"
#                                     (Conf/Loot/Fishing/Biome, .../Water and Conf/Fishing JSON,
#                                     plus DimensionFishFightRegistry + prefix on
#                                     FishingTableConverter.Convert for this mod's own fish)
#   SkillTalentsTableAuthoring        World Rules ▸ "What talents give" (Conf/Talents JSON)
# And what has no seam at all, so nothing is offered for it:
#   ActivatedContentBundlesAuthoring  the converter only makes an empty buffer; its contents are
#                                     runtime state the server syncs
#   WorldInfoAuthoring                the converter only makes an empty component; seed and name
#                                     live in the save
#   PugPrefabBufferAuthoring          the buffer belongs to the game's own carrier object, which a
#                                     mod cannot be; mod prefabs are converted anyway
#   PugDamagePrefabsAuthoring         dead vanilla code — nothing in the game reads it
#   InventoryAuxDataPrefabsAuthoring  a real seam (a postfix on InventoryAuxDataConverter.Convert)
#                                     but nothing needs custom container save data yet; recorded in
#                                     the capability registry as world-rules-container-aux-data
# ---- the player ----
# WITHDRAWN for the same reason: a mod's own player prefab loses the same race. What survives is
# World Rules ▸ "Overrides on the player", which writes over Core Keeper's own player object
# (ObjectID 6000) as a world converts it and puts the numbers back afterwards.
#   PlayerAuthoring                   turning delay and vehicle drift, overridden
#   PlayerAimPositionAuthoring        the aim offset, overridden
#   PlayerLocalAuthoring              engine wiring for the game's own singleton; nothing to author
#   PlayerCustomizationAuthoring      a placeholder the character creator overwrites before anyone
#                                     sees it, so setting it would do nothing a player could notice
#   EquippedObjectAuthoring           the slot handlers are pieces of the game's code, not values
# ---- per-object markers, all tickboxes on DimensionSimpleTraitsTemplate ----
ClientBiomeSamplesAuthoring
